events.description: With the release of sensor version 7.11, CrowdStrike introduced the new IPC Template Type, delivered as Rapid Response Content via Channel File 291; its definition expected 21 inputs but the sensor code supplied only 20.
IPC Template Type was tested with manual/automated tests (a static set of 12 test cases using wildcard matching in the 21st field) and a stress test; it passed and did not trigger a fault.
A first IPC Template Instance was released to production as Rapid Response Content; the first several field deployments were successful, all using wildcard matching for the 21st input.
Two additional IPC Template Instances were deployed, one introducing a non-wildcard matching criterion for the 21st input, producing a new version of Channel File 291.
The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances based on the expectation of 21 inputs and passed them; the new channel file was sent to sensors.

Windows sensors receiving the new Channel File 291 evaluated the Template Instances at the next IPC notification; accessing the 21st input value caused an out-of-bounds memory read and the system crashed (PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA bugcheck in csagent.sys).
As of this time, approximately 99% of Windows sensors were back online compared to before the content update (typical week-over-week variance is ~1%).
